correctness.finding: PASS. The finite-index lattice reduction is mathematically consistent. If q Z^2 is contained in Lambda, every nonnegative lattice point has a unique residue representative (i,j) in R and a unique pair of nonnegative quotient coordinates, giving the exact heat kernel K_Lambda(y)=sum_R exp(-y(iL+jM))/((1-exp(-qLy))(1-exp(-qMy)))-1. Expanding at zero gives the displayed c2,c1,c0, with c2=1/(hLM); the Mellin identity then gives the stated poles and Z_Lambda(0). The prime-index perturbation has the same summable remainder as Golafshan's unrestricted proof because each shell contains no more points than the full lattice, so the residue/saddle calculation transfers with the substituted lattice data. The collision identity for r^q,s^q,rs is exact: its exponent set is precisely A congruent to B modulo q. I independently simplified the diagonal-residue c0 formula and checked coefficient invariance for the same index-six lattice using q=6,12,18.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The result shows precisely how finite-index restrictions alter a recent strong prime-index counting theorem: the leading logarithmic constant depends only on the index through h^{-1/3}, while boundary arithmetic enters at lower orders. The collision corollary is useful because it prevents a false rank-three (log x)^{3/4} heuristic for dependent generators and identifies the correct two-dimensional distinct-index geometry.

limitations: The proof is a substantial but methodologically direct extension of the recent unrestricted analytic argument rather than a new saddle-point method.
The lattice, its index, and r,s are fixed; there is no uniformity for growing index and no treatment of affine or lower-rank exponent sets.
